questions.question: Carbon exhibits catenation property due to _____

options.text: its small size and greater strength of carbon-carbon bond
its large size and greater strength of carbon-carbon bond
its small size and weaker strength of carbon-carbon bond
its large size and weaker strength of carbon-carbon bond

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small size and greater strength of carbon-carbon bond.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon:**

 
 
• The chemical element carbon has the a**tomic number six **and the** symbol C.**
 
• It is **nonmetallic and tetravalent,** which means that because its valence shell has four electrons, its atoms can form up to four covalent bonds.
 
• It is a member of periodic table group 14.
 
• **It is a small atom with a small atomic radius, allowing it to form strong carbon- carbon covalent bonds.**
 
• The strength of the carbon-carbon bond allows for the formation of **long chains or rings**, which is the basis of** catenation.**
 
• The strength of the bond also makes carbon compounds **more stable** and **less reactive.**
 
• Different carbon atoms can form different bonds with one another to form different carbon allotropes. **Amorphous carbon, diamond, graphite, and fullerenes are a few examples of well-known allotropes.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Catenation:**

 
 
• **The capacity of certain elements to create bonds with atoms of the same element **is known as catenation, and it's a fascinating idea in chemistry.
 
• The great diversity and complexity of organic chemistry arise from this characteristic, which is especially noticeable in carbon compounds.
 
• **Catenation's greatest champion is carbon, which has four valence electrons. It easily forms strong covalent connections with other carbon atoms to form complex structures and lengthy chains.**
 
• Carbon may produce a variety of compounds, such as alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and aromatic compounds, by making single, double, and even triple bonds with itself.
 
• The c**atenation property of carbon is responsible for the amazing diversity of organic chemistry. **
 
• Other elements like **silicon and germanium** can also exhibit catenation, but their bonds are** not as strong** as carbon-carbon bonds.

questions.question: Which of the following falls under the Right to Constitutional Remedies?

options.text: Equality of opportunity in public employment
Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III is guaranteed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III is guaranteed.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies:**

 
 
• **Enshrined in the Part III: Fundamental Rights **of the Indian Constitution under **Article 32 **which **provides for the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III is guaranteed.**
 
• The **SC may issue directives, orders, or writs to enforce any of the fundamental rights** in accordance with Article 32.
 
• Among the **writs** that may be granted are: **Habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and Quo-warranto.**
 
• The **SC has original but not exclusive jurisdiction** over the enforcement of fundamental rights. It is **concurrent with the jurisdiction of the high court under Article 226.**
 
• The **right to move the SC cannot be suspended with the exception of Article 329** which states that in the **event of a national emergency, the President may revoke the ability to petition any court to enforce fundamental rights.**
 
• The **Supreme Court held in the Chandra Kumar case (1997) that the basic structure of the Constitution** includes the writ jurisdiction of both the high court and the Supreme Court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Right to Equality:

 
 
• **These are enshrined in Part III: Fundamental rights of the Indian Constitution under Article 14-18.**
 
• **Article 14:** No individual within the territory of India may be denied equality before the law or equal protection under the law on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• **Article 15:** No citizen may be subjected to discrimination by the State based only on their place of birth, race, caste, religion, or any of them.
 
• **Article 16: It ensures equality of opportunity in public work by prohibiting discrimination in public employment on the basis of sex, religion, race, caste, or place of birth.**
 
• **Article 17:** Abolition of untouchability and all forms of its practice .
 
• **Article 18: **All titles are abolished, with the exception of academic and military titles.
 
 
 
• **Rights to Freedom of Religion:**
 
 
• Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution are part of the Fundamental Rights which gives rights to freedom of religion.
 
• Article 25 guarantees the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• Article 26 grants every religious denomination the right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• Article 27 prohibits the state from compelling any person to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.
 
• Article 28 prohibits the imparting of religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of state funds.
 
 
 
• Right to Education:
 
 
• Article 21A, which reads, "The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of 6 to 14 years of age in such manner as the State, may by law determine," was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002.
 
• The original provisions for state-funded, equitable, and accessible education were found in Article 45, Part IV: Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Ramamurti Committee Report, 1990, was the first formal document establishing the right to an education.
 
• In the landmark ruling in Unnikrishnan JP versus State of Andhra Pradesh & Others (1993), the Supreme Court ruled that education is a fundamental right derived from Article 21.
 
• The establishment of the Tapas Majumdar Committee (1999) encompassed the addition of Article 21A.
 
• The right to education was made a **basic right in Part III: Fundamental Rights** of the Indian Constitution by the 86th Amendment, 2002.
 
• 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 also amended Article 45 of DPSP which now read as, "The state shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children untill they complete the age of six years."

questions.question: The magnification produced by a concave mirror is found to be -2 when an object of height 1 cm is placed at a suitable distance from the pole. Here, image height is equal to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 cm.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Given in the question:**

 
 
• The **magnification** produced by the **concave mirror (m) =** - 2, which means that the image formed is **Real and Inverted image.**
 
• **T**he height of the object **(h) = 1 cm.**
 
• The height of the image can be calculated using the formula, **m = h'/h**, where **h' is the height of the image.**
 
• From the above equation, we get,
 
• **h' = m x h = -2 x 1 cm =** **-2 cm.**
 
 
 
• Therefore,** the height of the image is** **2 cm **and** negative sign indicate that the image is inverted.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Concave Mirror:

 
 
• Mirror which has a depression towards the centre of sphere with polish opposite to the centre of curvature is called Concave mirror.
 
• This means that the mirror is curved inward, with the outer edges being closer to the viewer than the center.
 
• A concave mirror is also known as a converging mirror, as it focuses light rays that enter it towards a single point.
 
• The Centre of Curvature (C) and the Focus (f) are located in front of the mirror i.e. unpolished side.
 
 
 
• **Magnification** produced by a **concave mirror** is** negative** when the image formed is **Real and Inverted.**
 
• The height of the object is** equal** to the height of the image when the object is placed at the** focus **of the mirror.
 
• The** magnification** of a concave mirror can be calculated using the formula** m = -v/u**, where v is the distance of the image from the mirror and u is the distance of the object from the mirror.

questions.question: In the modern periodic table, addition of new shells down the group results in _______.

options.text: decrease in atomic size and nuclear charge

decrease in atomic size and increase in nuclear charge

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 Only**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The modern periodic table is arranged in such a way that elements are grouped based on their atomic number, which determines their chemical properties.
 
• As we move "down a group", a "new electron shell (energy level)" is added to each successive element.
 
• This results in a "gradual increase in atomic size" because the additional shell increases the distance between the nucleus and the outermost electrons.
 
• At the same time, the "nuclear charge (number of protons in the nucleus) increases" as we move down the group.
 
• However, despite the increasing nuclear charge, the "shielding effect" caused by the inner electron shells reduces the effective nuclear attraction on the outermost electrons.
 
• **Therefore, the correct answer is "Increase in atomic size and nuclear charge."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1 (Decrease in atomic size and nuclear charge) - Incorrect:** Atomic size "increases" as we move down the group, and nuclear charge also increases due to the addition of protons.
 
• **Option 2 (Increase in atomic size and decrease in nuclear charge) - Incorrect:** While atomic size increases, nuclear charge does "not" decrease. Instead, it increases because more protons are added to the nucleus.
 
• **Option 4 (Decrease in atomic size and increase in nuclear charge) - Incorrect:** Atomic size "does not decrease" down the group; it increases due to additional electron shells.

Thus, the correct answer is Option 3: Increase in atomic size and nuclear charge

• Reduction reactions are widely used in industrial processes such as the production of metals and organic chemicals.
 
 
 
• Redox reaction:

• **Gaining oxygen** would lead to an** increase in the oxidation state** of the substance.

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 21 minutes and 28 minutes, respectively. Both the pipes are opened together but after 4 minutes, pipe B is turned off. What is the total time taken to fill the tank?

Given: Pipe A alone can fill the tank in 21 minutes and Pipe B in 28 minutes.

The formula used: 

Tank capacity = time taken × efficiency

Calculations:-

Let the capacity of the tank be LCM(21, 28)

Capacity of tank = 84 unit

By using the formula,

The efficiency of Pipe A = frac{{Tank capacity}}{{Time Taken}} = (84)/(21) = 4

Efficiency of Pipe B = frac{{Tank capacity}}{{Time Taken}} = (84)/(28) = 3 

Let the time taken by Pipe A to fill the remaining tank be t,

Tank filled by both for 4 minutes + tank filled by A for t minutes = 84 units

⇒ (3 + 4) × 4 + t × 4 = 84

⇒ 7 × 4 + 4t = 84

⇒ 4t = 84 - 28 = 56 

⇒ t = 14

⇒ Total time = 14 + 4 =18

.·. The time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank is 18 minutes.

questions.question: The traffic signals at three different road crossings change after every 45 seconds, 75 seconds and 90 seconds respectively. If they all change simultaneously at 9:30:00 a.m., then at what time will they next change again simultaneously?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9:37:30 a.m.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Given in the question:**

 
 
• The traffic signals at three different road crossings change **after every 45 seconds, 75 seconds and 90 seconds respectively.**
 
• Now, The** time taken** for all three signals to change simultaneously again will be the **least common multiple** **(LCM) of 45, 75 and 90 seconds.**
 
• **After Prime factorizing** the numbers, we get
 
• 45 = 3 x 3 x 5,
 
• 75 = 3 x 5 x 5 
 
• 90 = 2 x 3 x 3 x 5.
 
• The LCM will have all the factors with their **highest powers**, so LCM = 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 x 5
 
• Thus, **LCM(45, 75, 90) = 450.**
 
 
 
• Therefore, the signals will next change simultaneously after **450 seconds, which is 7 minutes and 30 seconds** from 9:30:00 a.m., i.e. at **9:37:30 a.m**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Highest common factor:**

 
 
• **The largest positive integer that divides the numbers without leaving a residual is known as the greatest common divisor, or gcd, of two or more positive integers.**
 
• Consider the numbers 18 and 24. Since 6 is the greatest number that can divide both 18 and 24, the H.C.F. of 18 and 24 will equal 6.
 
 
 
• **Least common multiple:**
 
 
• The least common multiple, or LCM, of two numbers, let's say a and b, is represented in mathematics as LCM (a,b). **The smallest or least positive integer that is divisible by both a and b is known as the LCM.** Take the two positive integers 3 and 4, for instance.
 
• 3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,... are multiples of 3.
 
• 4,8,12,16,20,24,... are multiples of 4.
 
• For 3 and 4, the typical multiples are 12, 24, 36, 48, and so on. Twelve would be the least common multiple in the lot.
 
 
 
• **Product of Two numbers = (HCF of the two numbers) x (LCM of the two numbers)**

• It is also known as the **S**ingle Replacement Reaction.

 
 
• It **involves a more reactive element displacing a less reactive element from its compound.**
 
• The reaction of potassium with magnesium chloride is an example of a single displacement reaction.
 
 
• Reaction: 2K + MgCl2 → 2KCl + Mg
 
 
 
 
 
• In the given reaction, 2 Al atoms **replaces** the 2 Fe atoms in Fe2O3 to form Al2O₃ as **Aluminium (Al) is more reactive than Iron (Fe)**.

• It** involves two reactants exchanging their ions to form two new products.**
 
• For example, potassium nitrate reacts with aluminium chloride and forms aluminium nitrate and potassium chloride. 
 
 
• Reaction: KNO3 + AlCl3 ↔️ Al(NO3)3 + KCl

• The chemical reaction which involves addition of hydrogen or removal of oxygen is called reduction.

• Gaining hydrogen would lead to a decrease in the oxidation state of the substance.
 
• Losing oxygen would lead to a decrease in the oxidation state of the substance.

• In the nineteenth century, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, also called Ishwar Chandra Bandyopadhyay, was a well-known person in India.

questions.question: The refractive indices of dense flint glass and water are 1.65 and 1.33, respectively. A ray of light passes from dense flint glass to water. The refractive index of water with respect to dense flint glass is ______ and the ray bends _______ the normal in water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.81, away from**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• Given in the question:
 
 
• The** refractive index of water** **= 1.65**
 
• The** refractive index of dense flint glass = 1.33**
 
• The **refractive index of water with respect to dense flint glass = The refractive index of water / The refractive index of dense flint glass.**
 
• The refractive index of water with respect to dense flint glass = 1.33 / 1.65 = 0.81.
 
• Thus the **refractive index of water with respect to dense flint glass is** **0.81.**
 
• This indicates that water is rarer than dense flint glass.
 
• The ray of light bends** away from the normal **as it travels from water to dense flint glass.
 
 
 
• Thus,** the refractive index of water with respect to dense flint glass is 0.81 and the ray bends away from the normal in water.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In mathematical formulae and descriptive texts, the letter** n or n'** is most frequently used to represent the** refractive index variable.**
 
• Refracted light** bends more in the direction of the normal line when it moves from a less dense material to a denser one.**
 
• Refracted light** bends away from the normal line when it moves from a denser material to rarer medium.**

• It is classified as a hydroxy acid and is a carboxylic acid with the chemical formula C₃H₆O₃.
 
• It exists in two optical isomers: L-lactic acid and D-lactic acid.
 
• The accumulation of lactic acid in muscles is often associated with muscle fatigue and soreness, particularly during strenuous exercise.

• **Among the symptoms are restless or shaky, hungry, exhausted, lightheaded, dizzy, or agitated.**

questions.question: Which of the following part connects the urinary bladder and the kidney?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ureters.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**​****Ureters:**

__
 
• They are muscular tubes that** transport urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.**
 
• They extend from the renal pelvis of the kidney to the urinary bladder.
 
• **Each kidney has one ureter**, and the urine flows through the ureters by peristaltic contractions of the smooth muscle in the ureter walls.
 
• They have an **average length of about 25–30 centimeters** (10–12 inches).
 
• They have a one-way flow mechanism facilitated by the presence of valves called ureterovesical valves, which** prevent the backflow of urine **from the bladder into the ureters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Urethra:**

 
• It is a tubular structure that **serves as a duct for the passage of urine from the urinary bladder to the outside of the body.**
 
• **In males**, the urethra also has a reproductive function, **serving as the passage for semen** during ejaculation.
 
• The length and structure of the **urethra differ between males and females.**
 
• The female urethra is shorter and primarily serves the purpose of conducting urine from the bladder to the external urethral orifice.

**Nephrons:**

 
• They are the **structural and functional units of the kidneys**, which are vital organs **responsible for filtering blood, removing waste products,** and regulating various physiological processes in the body.
 
• Each **kidney contains approximately one million nephrons,** and these microscopic structures play a crucial role in maintaining the body's internal balance by regulating water and electrolyte levels and removing metabolic waste.
 
• Substances, such as** glucose, amino acids, and electrolytes, are reabsorbed from the filtrate** back into the bloodstream, primarily in the proximal convoluted tubule.
